text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanians arrested for smuggling cigarettes are called 'Russian Mafia' by German police.

- There are both poor and rich candidates to the Lithuanian parliament. The candidate with the biggest individual property and income of 1.5 million litas is A. Buzunas, a former secretary of President Algirdas Brazauskas.

- The second biggest Russian oil company JUKOS would like to buy 10 percent of shares (four million litas nominal price) of Klaipedos Nafta and to export two to three million tonnes of oil products via the terminal per year. Naftos Teriminalos, which controls 51 percent of Klaipedos Nafta, and Lancaster Steel Co.Inc., with 49 percent, agreed to sell the shares but government approval is still necessary.

- The government changed its decision of last week and approved Monday new conditions put forward by Merill Lynch for a $19 million credit to Mazheikiu Nafta to buy crude oil. Merrill will issue two credits of $9.5 million each with nine months maturity and a slightly higher than seven percent interest rate.

- Russia still has a strategy worked out that calls for the accupation of the Baltic countries if Russia's neighbours are taken into NATO, said Russian politologist and deputy director general of the U.S.A and Canada Institute Victor Kremeniuk.
- The state-owned shares of 27 enterprises will be put on auction at the stock exchange in November, the privatisation agency said.
- The stock exchange will begin publishing a share index of quoted companies this week.

- The Defence Ministry has bought light anti-tank guns from the Swedish Bofors company for $5 million, which will satisfy half of the needs of the defense system. The first consignment was delivered last weekend and the whole batch will reach military units in four months.

- Lithuanian, Estonian and Latvian Russians started discussions how to integrate themselves into local societies and to preserve their national identity in a three-day conference which started in Vilnius on Tuesday. There are 1.5 million people of Russian nationality residing in the Baltic countries.

- The Lithuanian embassy in Germany is among the few which is not a burden to the budget, says Lithuanian ambassador in Bonn, Zenonas Namavicius. The maintaince expenses of the embassy are one million DM while the embassy earns 1.5 million DM.

- The opposition Homeland Union (Conservatives) intends to amend the defence law to allow people of Lithuanian nationality who have served in NATO armies and receive pensions from those countries to become officers of the Lithuanian army and get officers rank.
